docs.text: Driver AS5047U Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the AS5047U 14-bit magnetic rotary position sensor. It reads the angle and the velocity over CRC-protected SPI frames, resolves the chip's error flags, sets the zero and the outputs, and burns the OTP, on any MCU. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that brings the bus up and moves bytes; it does the rest: the start-up wait for the chip's ready indication, the frame format and CRC, ERRFL handling and its latch, unit conversion and the OTP procedure. Magnetic rotary position sensor AS5047U ams OSRAM Function Absolute angle over 360°, 14 bits (16384 counts, 0.022° per count); velocity at 24.141 °/s per count; up to 28000 rpm Interface SPI mode 1, up to 10 MHz; 16-bit frames, or 24- and 32-bit frames with CRC-8 Compensation Dynamic angle error compensation (DAEC) and an adaptive velocity filter Integrity CRC-8 on frames; ERRFL error and warning flags; AGC and DIA for the magnet and the internal loops Outputs ABI quadrature (up to 4096 pulses per revolution), UVW commutation (1 to 7 pole pairs) and PWM Non-volatile memory One-time-programmable zero position and settings Supply 3.0 V to 3.6 V, or 4.5 V to 5.5 V through the on-chip LDO What you get ¶ One object per chip. AS5047U<YourPort> takes a reference to your port and does no I/O until EnsureInitialized() . See API guide . Errors you can act on. Every call returns Result<T> with an Error such as Bus , Crc or DeviceFault . See API guide . Datasheet defaults. Config{} holds the reset values of an unprogrammed part; a burned part is read back instead. See Configuration and OTP programming . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class checked by a concept: two bus hooks, plus optional delay (for the OTP burn) and logging hooks found at compile time. See Porting . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI. The host tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti . See Contract . Tested without hardware. Host tests run the driver against a register model of the chip. See Testing and CI . Where each part of the driver is in the datasheet: Datasheet map . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire the chip, write the port, read the angle in about 15 lines. API guide ¶ The driver's API by task, with code that compiles: initialise, measure, set the zero, watch the magnet, burn the OTP and handle errors. Datasheet sections this page relies on From ams OSRAM DS000637 v1-01: Adaptive velocity filter: Adaptive Filter System; Rotation Speed Measurement, p. 12 Angle, velocity, AGC, magnitude, ERRFL and DIA registers: Volatile Registers, p. 24 Settings, zero position and direction registers: Non-Volatile Registers (OTP), p. 27 AGC and the magnet's field strength: Automatic Gain Control (AGC) and CORDIC Magnitude, p. 37 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The shape of the API ¶ Group Calls Lifecycle EnsureInitialized() , IsInitialized() , Deinitialize() Configuration ApplyConfig() , GetConfig() , SetZeroPosition() , SetZeroHere() , SetDirection() Measurement ReadAngleCounts() , ReadAngleDegrees() , ReadAngleRadians() , ReadUncompensatedAngleCounts() , ReadVelocityCounts() , ReadVelocityDegPerSec() , ReadVelocityRpm() , ReadAgc() , ReadMagnitude() Diagnostics ReadDiagnostics() , ReadErrorFlags() , GetLastErrorFlags() , GetLatchedErrorFlags() , ClearLatchedErrorFlags() , GetLastReply() , ReadRegister() , WriteRegister() , ReadNonVolatile() OTP ProgramOtp() Free functions Validate() , CountsToDegrees() , CountsToRadians() , Crc8() , ToString() , GetDriverVersion() Every call that touches the chip returns Result<T> : check ok() (or the bool conversion) and read value , or read error . Result and Error are [[nodiscard]] , so an unchecked call is a compiler warning. A failed call's value is T{} , never a stale or partial reading. Initialise ¶ as5047u :: Error BringUp ( Sensor & sensor ) { // The one entry point: starts the chip on the first call, then returns Ok with no I/O. After a // failure the next call retries from the beginning. const auto r = sensor . EnsureInitialized (); if ( ! r ) { std :: printf ( "AS5047U init: %s 
 " , as5047u :: ToString ( r . error )); } return r . error ; } The constructor stores the port and the configuration and does no I/O. EnsureInitialized() is the one way to start the chip. Its first call brings the bus up and waits for the chip to be ready: it reads DIA once per millisecond, for at most Config::startup_timeout_ms (default t_pon, 10 ms; up to kStartupTimeoutMaxMs ), until every magnetic loop reports finished, and accepts that only when the next read says the same (datasheet "Timing Characteristics", Figure 9; DIA, Figure 35). A chip that is already up costs no wait. It then reads ERRFL once to clear what the power-up left there, writes the configuration and reads each register back. write_settings = false skips the writes, for an OTP-burned part, and reads the chip's settings into GetConfig() instead. Start-up result Meaning NoDevice Only line patterns until the deadline: MISO stuck or floating, MOSI looped back, DIA always 0 NotReady The chip answers, but its loops did not finish by the deadline (no magnet, slow supply) DeviceIdMismatch DIA has a bit set that reads 0 on an AS5047U: another device answers Once it has succeeded, EnsureInitialized() returns Ok at once with no I/O, so a caller (or a handler that owns the driver) can call it before every use. After a failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again from the beginning. No other call starts the chip: before EnsureInitialized() succeeds every read and write returns NotInitialized and sends nothing, so a read in a control loop is always its own frames and nothing more. ApplyConfig() before the start only stores the configuration for the first EnsureInitialized() . Deinitialize() only marks the driver uninitialised: the chip has no low-power mode. It is also the recovery after a fault: Deinitialize() , then EnsureInitialized() starts the chip again. Measure ¶ // One control-loop sample: angle and speed. Each read is two CRC-checked frames; two more only // when the chip flags the reply. A read under a magnet warning fails with MagnetWarning. bool Sample ( Sensor & sensor , float & angle_deg , float & speed_rpm ) { const auto a = sensor . ReadAngleDegrees (); const auto v = sensor . ReadVelocityRpm (); if ( ! a || ! v ) { return false ; // never use .value of a failed read: it is 0, not a measurement } angle_deg = a . value ; speed_rpm = v . value ; return true ; } Call Register Unit ReadAngleCounts() Address 0x3FFF: ANGLECOM, with DAEC unless dynamic_compensation is false; ANGLEUNC when uncompensated_at_angle_register is true 0 to 16383 counts, 0.022° per count ReadAngleDegrees() , ReadAngleRadians() Address 0x3FFF, as above [0, 360) °, [0, 2π) rad ReadUncompensatedAngleCounts() ANGLEUNC (0x3FFE): never compensated 0 to 16383 counts ReadVelocityCounts() VEL (0x3FFC), signed 14 bit 24.141 °/s per count ReadVelocityDegPerSec() , ReadVelocityRpm() VEL °/s, rpm ReadAgc() AGC (0x3FF9) 0 to 255 ReadMagnitude() MAG (0x3FFD), CORDIC magnitude 0 to 16383 Each read is two frames, CRC-checked unless the frame format is Bits16 , and nothing more while the reply carries no flag bit: this is the hot path, and no verification is ever added to it. When the reply carries the error or the warning bit, the driver reads ERRFL (two more frames) to find out why. An angle or velocity read under an AGC or magnetic-half warning fails with MagnetWarning : the field is out of the range the chip regulates, so the value is not a measurement (handbook KB-CPP-127). A P2RAM single-bit warning (corrected by the ECC) does not refuse it. Reply of an angle read Frames Result No flag bit 2 The angle Warning bit, ERRFL holds AGC_warning or MagHalf 4 MagnetWarning Warning bit, ERRFL holds only P2ram_warning 4 The angle Error bit 4 Crc , Framing , Command , DeviceFault ; NoDevice when ERRFL holds no error Error bit, ERRFL holds OffCompNotFinished or WDTST 18 DeviceReset when the settings registers changed, else DeviceFault ( below ) Error bit, the ERRFL read fails (CRC, transfer, reserved bit) 18 DeviceReset when the settings registers changed, else the read's error; flags_lost No flag bit, a compare is pending (it could not be read after a lost ERRFL) 16 The angle once the compare passes; DeviceReset on a difference; the compare's error while it cannot be read Two reads are two separate samples: the angle and the velocity of the example above are not taken at the same instant. The velocity reads ±1 count (±24 °/s) at standstill, and more with a high filter K: detect "stopped" with a threshold, not with zero. Set the zero and the direction ¶ as5047u :: Result < uint16_t > ZeroAtTheCurrentPosition ( Sensor & sensor ) { return sensor . SetZeroHere (); // the shaft's current position now reads 0 } SetZeroHere() writes the zero as 0, reads the angle, and writes that angle as the new zero; it returns the new zero position in counts. SetZeroPosition(counts) writes a known value, and SetDirection() chooses the direction in which the angle increases. Each reads the settings registers (to keep their diagnostic bits) and writes the whole configuration again. The settings are lost at power-off unless you burn them ( OTP programming ). Verify a write ¶ A write is the two frames the datasheet needs, the command and the data, always with a CRC, and the reply's error bit is checked as for every access. Reading the register back is chosen per call: WriteRegister() , ApplyConfig() , SetZeroPosition() , SetZeroHere() and SetDirection() take a last parameter as5047u::Verify , None by default. // Off a timed path (commissioning, a rarely changed setting): read the write back as well. as5047u :: Error SetDirectionChecked ( Sensor & sensor ) { // Two more frames per register; WriteMismatch if the chip lost the write. return sensor . SetDirection ( as5047u :: Direction :: CounterClockwise , as5047u :: Verify :: ReadBack ). error ; } Verify::ReadBack reads each written register back (two more frames per register) and fails with WriteMismatch when it differs: it catches a write the chip lost, or a read-only bit. Use it off the timed path; a call in a control loop stays at the frames the datasheet needs. Any other value is refused with InvalidArgument before any I/O. Two calls always read back, whatever you pass elsewhere: EnsureInitialized() (start-up is not timing-critical) and ProgramOtp() (a burn cannot be undone). A write that fails (a reply CRC error, a lost frame, an error flag, WriteMismatch ) may still have taken effect: the chip stores the data frame when it arrives. The driver never retries it. It reads DISABLE to ECC back (14 frames) and GetConfig() then holds what the chip holds, field by field. If that read fails too, the driver is uninitialised and EnsureInitialized() writes the configuration again. Watch the magnet ¶ Warnings refuse an angle or a velocity ( MagnetWarning ); the AGC, magnitude and diagnostics still read, so you can see why. ERRFL clears when it is read, and the driver reads it inside other calls; every value it reads, those included, is ORed into a latch the driver owns (handbook KB-CPP-119): Call I/O What it gives ReadErrorFlags() 2 frames ERRFL now (clears it on the chip; also ORed into the latch) GetLastErrorFlags() none The last ERRFL value the driver read, by any call GetLatchedErrorFlags() none Every ERRFL flag read since ClearLatchedErrorFlags() ; EnsureInitialized() empties it, then holds what the power-up left ClearLatchedErrorFlags() none Empties the latch, flags_lost included GetLastReply() none The raw reply word of the last frame, warning and error bits included bool MagnetIsHealthy ( Sensor & sensor ) { const auto agc = sensor . ReadAgc (); // mid-range is best: 0 too strong, 255 too weak const auto f = sensor . ReadErrorFlags (); // clears ERRFL on the chip; also ORed into the latch return agc && f && ! f . value . agc_warning && ! f . value . mag_half ; } // Everything ERRFL reported since the last check, including flags the driver's own reads // consumed (a read that failed with DeviceFault or MagnetWarning read ERRFL inside). No I/O. bool AnyFieldWarningSinceLastCheck ( Sensor & sensor ) { const as5047u :: ErrorFlags seen = sensor . GetLatchedErrorFlags (); sensor . ClearLatchedErrorFlags (); return seen . agc_warning || seen . mag_half ; } ReadDiagnostics() decodes DIA: the AGC limits ( agc_low , agc_high ), mag_half , whether the internal loops have settled ( loops_finished ), and whether the chip runs from 5 V ( vdd_5v ). Flag Meaning ErrorFlags::agc_warning AGC at 0 or 255: the magnet is too close or too far ErrorFlags::mag_half The field is at half the regulated value ErrorFlags::p2ram_warning The ECC corrected one bit of the OTP copy ErrorFlags::flags_lost In the latch only: a read of ERRFL failed (reply CRC, transfer, reserved bit) after its command may have reached the chip, which then cleared the flags it held: a fault may have been missed Reading ERRFL or AGC regularly is also what the datasheet requires for the AGC loop to work as specified. Notice a reset of the chip ¶ A power-on reset or a brown-out of the sensor (a supply dip, a loose connector) reloads DISABLE to ECC from the OTP: every setting written since start-up is gone ("Non-Volatile Registers (OTP)"), and on a blank part the zero and the direction return to their reset values, so the angle shifts with no error from the chip. The driver checks for this in two ways: Automatically , at no cost on the hot path: when any ERRFL read after start-up holds OffCompNotFinished or WDTST (the offset compensation restarts at power-up, Figure 33), or fails and so may have taken that flag, the driver reads DISABLE to ECC (14 frames) and compares them with what it last wrote or read there. On request : CheckForReset() makes the same comparison, 14 frames (about 34 µs of bus time at 10 MHz), for a supervision tick off the timed path. The datasheet does not promise that ERRFL holds the flag after a reset, so call it at the rate at which a reset must be noticed. On a difference the call fails with DeviceReset and the driver is uninitialised: no call writes the cached settings over the reset chip, and EnsureInitialized() starts it again with the stored configuration. A configuration equal to the OTP (a burned part with write_settings false, or Config{} on a blank part) is not changed by a reset, so nothing is reported and nothing is lost; the reads during t_pon after the reset still fail with DeviceFault . // A supervision tick, off the timed path: 14 frames. A reset of the chip (a supply dip) reloads // its settings from the OTP; the driver then reports DeviceReset, here or from any read whose // ERRFL says the offset compensation restarted, and EnsureInitialized() writes them again. as5047u :: Error Supervise ( Sensor & sensor ) { const auto r = sensor . CheckForReset (); if ( r . error == as5047u :: Error :: DeviceReset ) { return sensor . EnsureInitialized (). error ; } if ( sensor . GetLatchedErrorFlags (). flags_lost ) { std :: printf ( "an ERRFL read failed: a fault may have been missed 
 " ); sensor . ClearLatchedErrorFlags (); } return r . error ; } Use any register ¶ ReadRegister(address) reads any 14-bit address once, with no retry, and returns the 14 data bits; a warning bit alone does not fail it, an error bit is resolved through ERRFL. Reading ERRFL this way clears it on the chip and feeds the latch; reading DIA restarts its frame counter. WriteRegister(address, value) writes one (add Verify::ReadBack to read it back); it refuses PROG (0x0003) with InvalidArgument , so that only ProgramOtp() can start a burn. ReadNonVolatile() returns DISABLE to ECC (0x0015 to 0x001B) as an array, in address order. The addresses and fields are in inc/as5047u_registers.hpp ( as5047u::reg ). A WriteRegister() to a settings register is overwritten by the next ApplyConfig() . Burn the OTP ¶ as5047u :: Error BurnSettings ( Sensor & sensor ) { as5047u :: OtpReport report {}; // Irreversible. kOtpConfirm guards against a stray call. const auto r = sensor . ProgramOtp ( as5047u :: kOtpConfirm , report ); if ( ! r ) { std :: printf ( "OTP failed at step %u (burn %s) 
 " , static_cast < unsigned > ( report . failed_step ), report . burn_started ? "started: do not use the part" : "not started" ); } return r . error ; } Irreversible. ProgramOtp() needs the typed kOtpConfirm (an OtpBurnConfirm ; an integer does not compile), runs steps 6 to 19 of the datasheet procedure, and fills an OtpReport with the step that failed and whether the burn started. The steps before and after the call are yours. OTP programming has the whole procedure. Handle errors ¶ const char * Describe ( as5047u :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case as5047u :: Error :: Bus : case as5047u :: Error :: NoDevice : case as5047u :: Error :: DeviceIdMismatch : return "check the wiring, chip select, supply and SPI mode 1" ; case as5047u :: Error :: NotReady : return "the chip answers but its loops did not settle: supply, magnet, startup_timeout_ms" ; case as5047u :: Error :: MagnetWarning : return "magnet too far, too close or missing: check ReadAgc() and the air gap" ; case as5047u :: Error :: Crc : case as5047u :: Error :: Framing : return "signal integrity: lower the SPI clock, shorten the wires" ; case as5047u :: Error :: DeviceFault : return "chip fault or no magnet: check ReadErrorFlags() and ReadDiagnostics()" ; case as5047u :: Error :: DeviceReset : return "the chip was reset (supply dip?): call EnsureInitialized() again" ; default : return as5047u :: ToString ( e ); } } Signal Meaning What to do Error::Bus The port failed a transfer or the bus bring-up Check the port and the wiring; EnsureInitialized() again Error::NoDevice A reply a stuck, floating or looped-back line produces, at start-up or later Wiring, MISO, MOSI, supply ( Troubleshooting ) Error::NotReady At start-up the chip answered but its loops did not settle by startup_timeout_ms Magnet, supply ramp; raise the deadline Error::DeviceIdMismatch Something answered at start-up, but not an AS5047U (DIA bit 10 set) Chip select, the device on the bus Error::MagnetWarning An angle or velocity read under an AGC or magnetic-half warning: not a measurement Magnet distance and centring; ReadAgc() Error::Crc A reply had a wrong CRC, or the chip saw one (ERRFL.CRC_error) Lower the clock; shorten the wires Error::Framing The chip saw a frame of the wrong length (ERRFL.Framing_error) CSn must go high between frames; one transfer per frame Error::Command The chip saw an invalid command (ERRFL.Command_error) An unknown address in ReadRegister() or WriteRegister() Error::DeviceFault ERRFL reports a measurement fault: P2RAM, watchdog, CORDIC overflow, offset compensation Check the magnet and ReadDiagnostics() ; the value is not a measurement Error::DeviceReset The chip was reset (its settings registers no longer hold what the driver wrote) or a reset could not be ruled out; the driver is uninitialised Check the supply; EnsureInitialized() again ( Notice a reset ) Error::WriteMismatch A register read back different from what was written ( Verify::ReadBack , EnsureInitialized() or ProgramOtp() ) Read-only field, or a lost or corrupted write Error::Timeout The OTP burn did not finish in 100 ms OTP programming Error::OtpVerify The burned part failed the guard-band test Scrap the part Error::InvalidArgument A Config field or an argument is out of range; nothing was sent Fix the value ( Validate() ) Error::NotInitialized EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded Call it Error::Busy and Error::Unsupported belong to the shared base set but are never returned by this driver: the chip has no busy state and the driver no optional feature. Every value, with the calls that return it, is on the Contract page. as5047u::ToString() names an error for a log. Next: Configuration .

Reading the register back is chosen per call: WriteRegister() , ApplyConfig() , SetZeroPosition() , SetZeroHere() and SetDirection() take a last parameter as5047u::Verify , None by default. // Off a timed path (commissioning, a rarely changed setting): read the write back as well. as5047u :: Error SetDirectionChecked ( Sensor & sensor ) { // Two more frames per register; WriteMismatch if the chip lost the write. return sensor . SetDirection ( as5047u :: Direction :: CounterClockwise , as5047u :: Verify :: ReadBack ). error ; } Verify::ReadBack reads each written register back (two more frames per register) and fails with WriteMismatch when it differs: it catches a write the chip lost, or a read-only bit. Use it off the timed path; a call in a control loop stays at the frames the datasheet needs. Any other value is refused with InvalidArgument before any I/O. Two calls always read back, whatever you pass elsewhere: EnsureInitialized() (start-up is not timing-critical) and ProgramOtp() (a burn cannot be undone). A write that fails (a reply CRC error, a lost frame, an error flag, WriteMismatch ) may still have taken effect: the chip stores the data frame when it arrives. The driver never retries it. It reads DISABLE to ECC back (14 frames) and GetConfig() then holds what the chip holds, field by field. If that read fails too, the driver is uninitialised and EnsureInitialized() writes the configuration again.
docs.title: Verify a write

docs.text: Warnings refuse an angle or a velocity ( MagnetWarning ); the AGC, magnitude and diagnostics still read, so you can see why. ERRFL clears when it is read, and the driver reads it inside other calls; every value it reads, those included, is ORed into a latch the driver owns (handbook KB-CPP-119): Call I/O What it gives ReadErrorFlags() 2 frames ERRFL now (clears it on the chip; also ORed into the latch) GetLastErrorFlags() none The last ERRFL value the driver read, by any call GetLatchedErrorFlags() none Every ERRFL flag read since ClearLatchedErrorFlags() ; EnsureInitialized() empties it, then holds what the power-up left ClearLatchedErrorFlags() none Empties the latch, flags_lost included GetLastReply() none The raw reply word of the last frame, warning and error bits included bool MagnetIsHealthy ( Sensor & sensor ) { const auto agc = sensor . ReadAgc (); // mid-range is best: 0 too strong, 255 too weak const auto f = sensor . ReadErrorFlags (); // clears ERRFL on the chip; also ORed into the latch return agc && f && ! f . value . agc_warning && ! f . value . mag_half ; } // Everything ERRFL reported since the last check, including flags the driver's own reads // consumed (a read that failed with DeviceFault or MagnetWarning read ERRFL inside). No I/O. bool AnyFieldWarningSinceLastCheck ( Sensor & sensor ) { const as5047u :: ErrorFlags seen = sensor . GetLatchedErrorFlags (); sensor . ClearLatchedErrorFlags (); return seen . agc_warning || seen . mag_half ; } ReadDiagnostics() decodes DIA: the AGC limits ( agc_low , agc_high ), mag_half , whether the internal loops have settled ( loops_finished ), and whether the chip runs from 5 V ( vdd_5v ). Flag Meaning ErrorFlags::agc_warning AGC at 0 or 255: the magnet is too close or too far ErrorFlags::mag_half The field is at half the regulated value ErrorFlags::p2ram_warning The ECC corrected one bit of the OTP copy ErrorFlags::flags_lost In the latch only: a read of ERRFL failed (reply CRC, transfer, reserved bit) after its command may have reached the chip, which then cleared the flags it held: a fault may have been missed Reading ERRFL or AGC regularly is also what the datasheet requires for the AGC loop to work as specified.
docs.title: Watch the magnet

docs.text: A power-on reset or a brown-out of the sensor (a supply dip, a loose connector) reloads DISABLE to ECC from the OTP: every setting written since start-up is gone ("Non-Volatile Registers (OTP)"), and on a blank part the zero and the direction return to their reset values, so the angle shifts with no error from the chip. The driver checks for this in two ways: Automatically , at no cost on the hot path: when any ERRFL read after start-up holds OffCompNotFinished or WDTST (the offset compensation restarts at power-up, Figure 33), or fails and so may have taken that flag, the driver reads DISABLE to ECC (14 frames) and compares them with what it last wrote or read there. On request : CheckForReset() makes the same comparison, 14 frames (about 34 µs of bus time at 10 MHz), for a supervision tick off the timed path. The datasheet does not promise that ERRFL holds the flag after a reset, so call it at the rate at which a reset must be noticed. On a difference the call fails with DeviceReset and the driver is uninitialised: no call writes the cached settings over the reset chip, and EnsureInitialized() starts it again with the stored configuration. A configuration equal to the OTP (a burned part with write_settings false, or Config{} on a blank part) is not changed by a reset, so nothing is reported and nothing is lost; the reads during t_pon after the reset still fail with DeviceFault . // A supervision tick, off the timed path: 14 frames. A reset of the chip (a supply dip) reloads // its settings from the OTP; the driver then reports DeviceReset, here or from any read whose // ERRFL says the offset compensation restarted, and EnsureInitialized() writes them again. as5047u :: Error Supervise ( Sensor & sensor ) { const auto r = sensor . CheckForReset (); if ( r . error == as5047u :: Error :: DeviceReset ) { return sensor . EnsureInitialized (). error ; } if ( sensor . GetLatchedErrorFlags (). flags_lost ) { std :: printf ( "an ERRFL read failed: a fault may have been missed \n " ); sensor . ClearLatchedErrorFlags (); } return r . error ; }
docs.title: Notice a reset of the chip

docs.text: ReadRegister(address) reads any 14-bit address once, with no retry, and returns the 14 data bits; a warning bit alone does not fail it, an error bit is resolved through ERRFL. Reading ERRFL this way clears it on the chip and feeds the latch; reading DIA restarts its frame counter. WriteRegister(address, value) writes one (add Verify::ReadBack to read it back); it refuses PROG (0x0003) with InvalidArgument , so that only ProgramOtp() can start a burn. ReadNonVolatile() returns DISABLE to ECC (0x0015 to 0x001B) as an array, in address order. The addresses and fields are in inc/as5047u_registers.hpp ( as5047u::reg ). A WriteRegister() to a settings register is overwritten by the next ApplyConfig() .

docs.text: as5047u :: Error BurnSettings ( Sensor & sensor ) { as5047u :: OtpReport report {}; // Irreversible. kOtpConfirm guards against a stray call. const auto r = sensor . ProgramOtp ( as5047u :: kOtpConfirm , report ); if ( ! r ) { std :: printf ( "OTP failed at step %u (burn %s) \n " , static_cast < unsigned > ( report . failed_step ), report . burn_started ? "started: do not use the part" : "not started" ); } return r . error ; } Irreversible. ProgramOtp() needs the typed kOtpConfirm (an OtpBurnConfirm ; an integer does not compile), runs steps 6 to 19 of the datasheet procedure, and fills an OtpReport with the step that failed and whether the burn started. The steps before and after the call are yours. OTP programming has the whole procedure.

The chip answers a frame during the next one (dashed arrows), so a read sends the read command and then a NOP read, whose reply carries the register. The reply in the first frame belongs to the frame before it, so the driver fails the call there only when the transfer itself fails. When the reply that answers the call has its error bit set, the driver reads ERRFL (two more frames, dashed) to find out why and fails the call. A write sends the command frame (R/W at 0, the address) and the data frame, always with a CRC; the reply in the data frame reports on the command frame. The read-back after it (two more frames, dashed) is chosen per call with Verify::ReadBack; EnsureInitialized() and ProgramOtp() always read back. The frame words come from readRaw(), writeRaw() and resolveFlags() in src/as5047u.ipp. A note at the bottom gives the rule of FrameBus::Exchange(): after a failed transfer the next frame is a NOP read, so a lost data frame cannot turn the next command into data. Design choices ¶ CRTP, not virtual functions. The port is a template parameter constrained by the SpiPort concept, so every call is resolved at compile time and a missing hook is a compile error that names it. Exact port concepts. SpiPort matches each hook's address with detail::ExactHook<Port, Sig> , which takes a member function of exactly that noexcept signature and converts no value: a narrowed length or a throwing hook is a compile error, not a silent truncation. Hooks by named concepts. DelayUs and Log are detected by Declares* / Has* concepts in one place. A missing DelayUs() fails to compile at EnsureInitialized() , a missing Log() logs nothing, a misdeclared one is a compile error; none is skipped silently. The frame layer belongs to the driver. The port moves bytes; the driver builds every frame, computes and checks the CRC and sends writes as CRC-protected frames whatever the read format. A flagged reply is resolved, never ignored. The reply's error bit fails the call after ERRFL says why. Its warning bit refuses an angle or a velocity when ERRFL holds a field warning ( MagnetWarning ): a reading the chip says is under an out-of-range field is not a measurement. Every ERRFL value read goes into a latch, so no internal read hides a flag. Ready means confirmed. Start-up waits for DIA to report every loop finished, twice in a row, with a deadline from Config ; a stuck or looped-back line cannot fake it. A lean angle read. Two frames and one test of the flag bits; a flagged reply costs two more. Verification that adds frames ( Verify::ReadBack ) is chosen per call and never applies to reads. CRC by table. Crc8() uses a 256-byte constexpr table, two lookups per word instead of 16 shift-and-XOR steps, checked against the bitwise definition at compile time and for all 65 536 words in a test. On the host the CRC is about three times faster per word (14 ns against 40 to 65 ns on a 64-bit host at -O2 ), and a 24-bit angle read with a stub port went from 13 to 70 ns to 6 to 16 ns across GCC 15 and Clang; a 16-bit read, which has no CRC, stays within a few nanoseconds of before. Either way the bus dominates: two 24-bit frames take 4.8 µs at 10 MHz. On a target the table costs 256 bytes of flash (read-only data); not measured on an MCU yet. No I/O in the constructor. Construction cannot fail, so the driver can be a static or a member of a handler. One error type. Result<T> carries a value and an Error ; nothing throws and nothing returns a bare bool . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no printf . The driver is a header-only template with no mutable static state. docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. Entries under Breaking need source changes in code that used the affected API. [Unreleased] ¶ Changed ¶ The repository moved to kokeb-labs-drivers; URLs follow. The Hardware page draws the chip from the new docs/hardware.yml : the TSSOP-14 pinout with each pin's port hook, the block diagram of Figure 2, the minimum circuit of Figure 61 (5 V) and the 3.3 V supply option of Figure 11, and the pin and parts tables, every fact with its datasheet section and page. TEST, which Figure 4 gives no pin type, is marked as not confirmed. The hand-written pin table is gone. The hardware-lessons-review skill and tools/preflight.sh follow the template. [0.1.0] - 2026-11-09 ¶ Breaking ¶ A reset of the chip is reported as the new Error::DeviceReset (23). When an ERRFL read after start-up holds OffCompNotFinished or WDTST, the driver reads DISABLE to ECC (14 frames) and compares them with what it last wrote or read there; on a difference, or when that read cannot be completed, the call (an angle or register read, a setter, ReadErrorFlags() ) fails with DeviceReset instead of DeviceFault , and the driver is uninitialised until EnsureInitialized() writes the configuration again. Before, a power-on reset that reloaded the OTP went unnoticed: the angle moved with the lost zero and direction, the reads succeeded and GetConfig() still showed the old settings. A switch over Error with -Wswitch-enum needs the new case. A failed settings write is read back, not assumed. A write whose reply failed (a CRC error, a lost frame, an error flag, a read-back mismatch) may still have reached the chip. ApplyConfig() and the setters used to restore the old configuration in GetConfig() . Now they read DISABLE to ECC back (14 frames) and GetConfig() takes every chip field from what the chip holds. The write is never retried. When that read fails too, the driver is uninitialised and EnsureInitialized() writes the configuration again. A failed WriteRegister() to a settings register reads the registers back the same way, for the reset check. An angle or velocity under a magnet warning is refused. When the reply carries the warning bit and ERRFL holds AGC_warning or MagHalf, ReadAngleCounts() , ReadUncompensatedAngleCounts() , ReadAngleDegrees() , ReadAngleRadians() and the velocity reads fail with the new Error::MagnetWarning instead of returning the value (handbook KB-CPP-127): the chip says the field is out of the range it regulates. Before, warnings never failed a read. A P2RAM single-bit warning (corrected by the ECC) still returns the value; AGC, magnitude and diagnostics read as before. Such a read costs four frames (the ERRFL read); a read whose reply has no flag bit stays two. Start-up waits for the chip to be ready. EnsureInitialized() polls DIA once per millisecond until every loop reports finished, confirmed by a second read, for at most the new Config::startup_timeout_ms (default 10 ms, t_pon; 0 to kStartupTimeoutMaxMs = 1000). A chip that answers but is not ready fails with the new Error::NotReady ; before, any non-zero DIA started the driver (handbook KB-CPP-124). Stuck lines are NoDevice . A missing chip, MISO stuck low or floating high, a looped-back MOSI or a chip that cannot hear MOSI now fail with the new Error::NoDevice (20) instead of DeviceIdMismatch , at start-up and, for a line pattern with a wrong CRC, an ERRFL with its reserved bit set or an error bit with no error in ERRFL, on later reads (handbook KB-CPP-116, KB-CPP-047). DeviceIdMismatch now means only that DIA has a bit set that reads 0 on an AS5047U. An absent chip is reported after the start-up deadline (10 ms by default), not at once. Every port needs DelayUs() , because start-up polls DIA: a port without it no longer compiles, also when it never calls ProgramOtp() . The port concept checks exact hook signatures and noexcept . A Transfer() with a length narrower than std::size_t , a hook without noexcept , a DelayUs() that does not take uint32_t or a Log() with another signature is a compile error. ProgramOtp() takes an OtpBurnConfirm . kOtpConfirm is now that type, so ProgramOtp(kOtpConfirm, report) compiles unchanged; passing an integer does not compile. Error is [[nodiscard]] : a call whose Error is dropped (for example Validate(config); ) warns. GetConfig() on a temporary driver is deleted (the reference would dangle). Added ¶ CheckForReset() : the same comparison on request, 14 frames, for a periodic check where a reset must not go unnoticed (the datasheet does not promise the ERRFL flag after a reset). ErrorFlags::flags_lost , set in GetLatchedErrorFlags() when a read of ERRFL fails after its command may have reached the chip (a reply CRC error, a failed transfer, NoDevice for the reserved bit): ERRFL clears when read, so the flags it held may have been missed. ClearLatchedErrorFlags() and EnsureInitialized() clear it. Such a read may have taken a reset's OffCompNotFinished, so it also makes the driver compare the settings registers (14 frames; DeviceReset on a difference). When that compare cannot be read either, it stays pending and every later call fails with its error until it is read: no value is returned while a reset may have gone unseen. docs.text: Configuration ¶ Every field of as5047u::Config , the register it goes to, how a configuration is checked, OTP-burned parts, and the optional Kconfig layer. Datasheet sections this page relies on From ams OSRAM DS000637 v1-01: Dynamic angle error compensation (DAEC): Dynamic Angle Error Compensation, p. 12 Adaptive velocity filter: Adaptive Filter System; Rotation Speed Measurement, p. 12 Settings, zero position and direction registers: Non-Volatile Registers (OTP), p. 27 ABI incremental output: ABI Incremental Interface, p. 31 UVW commutation output: UVW Commutation Interface, p. 33 PWM output and hysteresis: PWM; Incremental Output Hysteresis, p. 35 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Fields ¶ Config{} holds the register reset values of a part whose OTP was never burned (every non-volatile register reads 0), so it changes nothing on such a chip. Only the frame format is a driver-side choice. EnsureInitialized() and ApplyConfig() read DISABLE to ECC, to keep the diagnostic bits of ZPOSL and SETTINGS1, and write DISABLE to SETTINGS3 (0x0015 to 0x001A). EnsureInitialized() reads each write back; ApplyConfig() does only with Verify::ReadBack ( API guide ). The writes go to the volatile copy and are lost at power-off unless you burn them ( OTP programming ). Field Default Range Register frame FrameFormat::Bits24 Bits16 , Bits24 , Bits32 Driver only: the frame length of reads. Bits16 reads carry no CRC : MISO stuck low reads as angle 0 with no flag ( Status and limitations ) pad_byte 0 0 to 255 Driver only: the pad byte of 32-bit frames write_settings true Driver only: false leaves the settings as the chip has them startup_timeout_ms 10 ( kPowerOnTimeMs , t_pon) 0 to 1000 ( kStartupTimeoutMaxMs ) Driver only: how long EnsureInitialized() polls DIA for the chip to be ready; 0 checks once direction Direction::Clockwise Clockwise , CounterClockwise SETTINGS2.DIR zero_position 0 0 to 16383 counts ZPOSM (bits 13..6), ZPOSL (bits 5..0) dynamic_compensation true SETTINGS2.DAECDIS = 0 adaptive_filter true DISABLE.FILTER_disable = 0 filter_k_min_code 0 0 to 7 SETTINGS1.K_min filter_k_max_code 0 0 to 7 SETTINGS1.K_max incremental IncrementalOutput::Abi Abi , Uvw SETTINGS2.UVW_ABI abi_enable true DISABLE.ABI_off = 0 uvw_enable true DISABLE.UVW_off = 0 pwm_enable false SETTINGS2.PWMon abi_resolution_code 0 0 to 7 SETTINGS3.ABIRES abi_decimal false SETTINGS2.ABI_DEC index_width IndexWidth::ThreeLsb ThreeLsb , OneLsb SETTINGS2.IWIDTH uvw_pole_pairs 1 1 to 7 SETTINGS3.UVWPP + 1 hysteresis_code 0 0 to 3 SETTINGS3.HYS high_temperature_noise false SETTINGS2.NOISESET: 150 °C operation at 3.3 V uncompensated_at_angle_register false SETTINGS2.Data_select: address 0x3FFF and the PWM output carry the angle without DAEC Directions are seen from above the magnet. The driver keeps the diagnostic enable bits of ZPOSL and SETTINGS1 (Dia1_en to Dia4_en) as the chip has them. With uncompensated_at_angle_register false (the reset value) address 0x3FFF reads ANGLECOM, the compensated angle; ReadUncompensatedAngleCounts() reads ANGLEUNC (0x3FFE) in either case. ECC is written only by ProgramOtp() . Codes are the raw register field values (Figures 46 to 48), not physical values: Filter. The velocity filter picks a coefficient K between K_min and K_max from the acceleration; low K means less noise and more latency. The code-to-K mapping is not linear (Figure 13): K_min code 0 is K = 2, K_max code 0 is K = 6. The application note AS5x47U Adaptive Filter helps choose them. DAEC. Dynamic angle error compensation removes the latency of the angle at speed. The datasheet suggests turning it off below about 100 rpm, where it only adds noise. ABI resolution. With abi_decimal false: abi_resolution_code Steps per revolution Pulses per revolution 0 (default) 4096 1024 1 2048 512 2 1024 256 3 8192 2048 4 16384 4096 With abi_decimal true the codes give decimal counts, from 1000 down to 25 pulses per revolution; the datasheet's SETTINGS3 table (Figure 48) lists them, and the codes not shown here. Outputs. incremental picks ABI or UVW on the shared pins; abi_enable and uvw_enable tristate the pins when false; PWM goes on pin W with ABI and on pin I with UVW ( Hardware ). Start from Config{} and change fields: as5047u :: Config EncoderConfig () { as5047u :: Config c {}; // reset values of an unprogrammed part c . direction = as5047u :: Direction :: CounterClockwise ; c . abi_resolution_code = 4 ; // 14-bit ABI: 4096 pulses per revolution c . uvw_pole_pairs = 7 ; // BLDC commutation for a 7-pole-pair motor return c ; // as5047u::Validate(c) checks it without touching the chip } as5047u :: Error StartAsEncoder ( MyPort & port ) { static as5047u :: AS5047U < MyPort > sensor ( port , EncoderConfig ()); // stored, no I/O return sensor . EnsureInitialized (). error ; // InvalidArgument if the config is out of range } Validation ¶ as5047u::Validate(config) checks a configuration without touching the chip, and EnsureInitialized() and ApplyConfig() call it before any I/O. It returns Error::InvalidArgument when an enum holds a value that is not an enumerator, zero_position is above 16383, a 3-bit code is above 7, hysteresis_code is above 3, or uvw_pole_pairs is 0 or above 7. Change one setting ¶ SetZeroPosition() , SetZeroHere() and SetDirection() change one field of GetConfig() and write it with ApplyConfig() , so every other field is written again with the value it already has. SetZeroHere() sets the zero to 0, reads the angle and writes it as the new zero: steps 4 and 5 of the datasheet's OTP procedure. OTP-burned parts ¶ A part whose OTP is burned starts from its own settings. Initialise it with write_settings = false : the driver checks that the chip answers, writes nothing, and reads DISABLE to SETTINGS3 back into GetConfig() . as5047u :: Error StartBurnedPart ( as5047u :: AS5047U < MyPort >& sensor ) { as5047u :: Config c {}; c . write_settings = false ; // keep what the OTP holds and read it into GetConfig() if ( auto r = sensor . ApplyConfig ( c ); ! r ) { // before the start: stored, no I/O return r . error ; } return sensor . docs.text: Contract ¶ What the AS5047U driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() brings the bus up and waits for the chip: it polls DIA once per millisecond, for at most Config::startup_timeout_ms (default t_pon, 10 ms), until every magnetic loop reports finished, and accepts that only when the next DIA read confirms it. A DIA that is all zeros or all ones, or a line pattern with a wrong CRC, is NoDevice ; a DIA with a bit set that reads 0 on an AS5047U is DeviceIdMismatch ; a chip that answers but is not ready by the deadline is NotReady . Then it reads ERRFL once to clear what the power-up left (the value goes into the latch), and only then writes the configuration and reads it back. With write_settings = false it writes nothing and reads the chip's settings into GetConfig() . On any failure the driver stays uninitialised. Every call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds. No call initialises the chip as a side effect. Every port failure propagates as Error::Bus ; a failed read returns T{} , never a stale or partial value. After a failed transfer the next frame is a read of NOP, because the chip may still be waiting for the data frame of a write: taken as a command it reads nothing, taken as data it writes 0 (for PROG: no burn). A register whose write failed holds an unknown value (the old one, the new one or 0), so a failed ApplyConfig() or setter never retries the write and never keeps the old or the new value: it reads DISABLE to ECC back (14 frames, CRC- and flag-checked) and GetConfig() takes every chip field from what the chip holds; when that read fails too, the driver is uninitialised and EnsureInitialized() writes the configuration again. For ZPOSL and SETTINGS1 that 0 includes their DIA enable bits, which ApplyConfig() keeps as the chip holds them: power-cycle the chip (they reload from the OTP) or write them back with WriteRegister() if they matter to you. Every reply's CRC is checked (24- and 32-bit frames), and every reply's error bit is resolved through ERRFL: Crc , Framing , Command or DeviceFault . A reply that a stuck, floating or looped-back line produces is never a value: all zeros or all ones with a wrong CRC, an ERRFL with its reserved bit set, or an error bit with no error in ERRFL is NoDevice (handbook KB-CPP-116). An angle or velocity whose reply carries the warning bit is returned only when ERRFL holds no field warning; with an AGC or magnetic-half warning the call fails with MagnetWarning (handbook KB-CPP-127). A P2RAM single-bit warning (corrected by the ECC) does not refuse it. Other reads return their value under a warning. Every ERRFL value the driver reads, its own internal reads included, is ORed into one latch: GetLatchedErrorFlags() (no I/O) until ClearLatchedErrorFlags() (handbook KB-CPP-119). A read of ERRFL that fails once its command may have reached the chip (a reply CRC error, a failed transfer, the reserved bit set) sets flags_lost in the latch: ERRFL clears when read, so a fault may have been missed, a reset's OffCompNotFinished included. The driver then compares the settings registers as below (14 frames). When that compare cannot be read either, the call keeps its own error, the driver stays initialised and the compare stays pending: every later call runs it after its own access (14 more frames) and fails with the compare's error ( Bus , Crc , ...) until it can be read, so no value is returned while a reset may have gone unseen. A compare that is read ends it: DeviceReset on a difference, else the call's own result. A reset of the chip is never followed by the old cached settings. When an ERRFL read after start-up holds OffCompNotFinished or WDTST, the driver reads DISABLE to ECC (14 frames) and compares them with what it last wrote or read there; on a difference, or when that read cannot be completed, the call fails with DeviceReset and the driver is uninitialised until EnsureInitialized() writes the configuration again. CheckForReset() makes the same comparison on request. An angle or velocity read is two frames when the reply has no flag bit set, four when it has one (the ERRFL read), and 18 when that ERRFL holds OffCompNotFinished or WDTST or its read fails (the settings check). Nothing else is ever added to it, except the pending compare described above (16 frames: the read and the compare) after a failed ERRFL read whose compare failed too. The compare covers the bits each register implements (DISABLE 6..0, the others 7..0, Figures 43 to 49). Every write is CRC-protected, in every frame format. A run-time write ( WriteRegister() , ApplyConfig() , the setters) is the command and data frames only, unless the call passes Verify::ReadBack ; EnsureInitialized() reads every settings write back. Every frame of ProgramOtp() , reads included, is CRC-protected, and its writes of steps 7, 9, 12 and 15 are always read back. The only waits are in EnsureInitialized() (1 ms between polls of DIA, at most Config::startup_timeout_ms , at most kStartupTimeoutMaxMs ) and in ProgramOtp() (1 ms between polls of the burn, at most kOtpBurnTimeoutMs , 100 ms). Every loop has a fixed bound. ProgramOtp() takes a typed OtpBurnConfirm , burns nothing without kOtpConfirm , sends the burn command once and never retries it, and WriteRegister() refuses PROG. Config{} equals the register reset values of an unprogrammed part. The port concept checks each hook's exact signature and noexcept : a hook with a narrower parameter or without noexcept is a compile error. A missing DelayUs() is a compile error at EnsureInitialized() ; a missing Log() logs nothing; a misdeclared DelayUs() or Log() is a compile error. What the chip needs from the bus is constexpr in inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp ( kSpiMode to kContinuousWord ), for a port to static_assert against. Deinitialize() does no I/O: the chip has no low-power mode. Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the port CMake 3.16 or later Generates as5047u_version.h Your port The bus, within the bus requirements; the delay; optionally logging ( Porting ) Nothing else: no RTOS, no SDK, no other repository of the org. Threading ¶ The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Use each driver object from one task at a time, or guard every call on it with one mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock, and the bus lock when several chips share a bus. Nothing may run in an ISR: every call can block for a bus transfer or a delay. Separate objects share no state. Errors ¶ as5047u::Error inside as5047u::Result<T> . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; this driver returns all of them except Busy and Unsupported , plus eight chip-specific values. Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded, or Deinitialize() ran since InvalidArgument 2 A Config field or argument is out of range ( Validate() , a Verify that is not an enumerator, a startup_timeout_ms above kStartupTimeoutMaxMs ), WriteRegister() on PROG, or ProgramOtp() without kOtpConfirm ; nothing was sent Bus 3 A port hook returned false Timeout 4 The OTP burn did not finish in kOtpBurnTimeoutMs (100 ms) DeviceIdMismatch 5 Something answers at EnsureInitialized() , but DIA has bit 10 set, which reads 0 on an AS5047U Crc 6 A reply's CRC was wrong, or ERRFL.CRC_error is set (the chip saw a wrong CRC) Busy 7 Never returned: the chip has no busy state DeviceFault 8 ERRFL reports P2RAM_error, Watchdog_error, Off_comp_error or CORDIC_overflow Unsupported 9 Never returned: the driver has no optional feature Framing 16 ERRFL.Framing_error is set: the chip saw a frame of the wrong length Command 17 ERRFL.Command_error is set: the chip saw an invalid command WriteMismatch 18 A register read back different from what was written: a call with Verify::ReadBack , EnsureInitialized() , or OTP steps 7, 9, 11, 12 and 15 OtpVerify 19 The OTP guard-band read-back differs from what was burned (OTP step 19) NoDevice 20 A reply a stuck, floating or looped-back line produces: only such replies at start-up until the deadline, or at run time a line pattern with a wrong CRC, an ERRFL with its reserved bit 8 set, or an error bit with no error in ERRFL NotReady 21 At EnsureInitialized() : the chip answers, but DIA did not report every loop finished (twice in a row) by Config::startup_timeout_ms MagnetWarning 22 An angle or velocity reply carried the warning bit and ERRFL holds AGC_warning or MagHalf: the field is out of range and the value is not a measurement DeviceReset 23 The chip was reset, or a reset could not be ruled out: after OffCompNotFinished or WDTST in ERRFL, or in CheckForReset() , the settings registers did not hold what the driver wrote (or could not be read after such a flag). The driver is uninitialised The API guide says what to do about each. Memory ¶ No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. A driver object holds a reference to the port, a Config , the last reply word, the last ERRFL value, the ERRFL latch, the 14-byte copy of the settings registers it compares a reset against and five flags: under 80 bytes. Stack use is small and fixed: 4-byte frame buffers, and 14-byte register arrays in ReadNonVolatile() , CheckForReset() and ProgramOtp() . The CRC-8 table is 256 bytes of read-only data. Platform ¶ Platform-free: the same code runs on any target with a C++20 compiler, including the host tests. The ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example, not part of the driver. Deviations from the standard ¶ None.

Bus settings ¶ Setting Value SPI mode 1: CPOL = 0, CPHA = 1. The chip samples MOSI on the falling edge of CLK. Modes 0, 2 and 3 do not work Clock Up to 10 MHz (t_clk ≥ 100 ns) Bit order MSB first Chip select Active low, one frame per low period. CSn must go high between frames: the chip finds the frame length from the CSn low time and executes the frame on the rising edge Reply The reply to a frame arrives during the next frame Driver default 24-bit frames with CRC-8 ( FrameFormat::Bits24 ) Frames ¶ "SPI Transaction" section, Figures 20 to 28. RW is 1 for a read and 0 for a write. Format MOSI (host to chip) MISO (chip to host) Driver 16 bit [14] RW = 1, [13:0] address [15] warning, [14] error, [13:0] data Bits16 : reads only, no CRC 24 bit [22] RW, [21:8] address or data, [7:0] CRC [23] warning, [22] error, [21:8] data, [7:0] CRC Bits24 : the default 32 bit [31:24] pad, then the 24-bit frame The 24-bit frame, then [7:0] pad Bits32 : daisy chains, pad from Config::pad_byte SPI frames, bit by bit Figure description and sources Each frame is drawn in the order it is clocked, most significant bit first, and the numbers above a row are bit positions in that frame. On MOSI the 16-bit command word holds the R/W bit (1 to read, 0 to write) and a 14-bit address; the data frame of a write has the same layout with R/W at 0 and the 14-bit value in place of the address. On MISO the reply word holds the warning bit, the error bit (a flag is set in ERRFL) and 14 data bits. The 24-bit frame adds the CRC-8 of the word in both directions. The 32-bit frame adds the pad byte: first on MOSI (the driver sends Config::pad_byte), last on MISO (the driver ignores it). The bit positions come from the frame constants in inc/as5047u_registers.hpp and the byte order from detail::FrameBus::Exchange in inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp. With 16-bit frames the driver sends writes as 24-bit frames. Drawn from: inc/as5047u_registers.hpp frame bits ; inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp detail::FrameBus::Exchange ; inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp Crc8 ; inc/as5047u.hpp writeFormat ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/spi-frames.py . The datasheet allows 16-bit frames for reads only, so with Bits16 the driver sends every write as a 24-bit frame. Writes are always CRC-protected, and ProgramOtp() sends every frame, reads included, as a 24-bit frame whatever Config::frame says, then restores the format. The CRC is CRC-8 with polynomial 0x1D, initial value 0xC4 and final XOR 0xFF, over the 16-bit word ("CRC Checksum"); as5047u::Crc8() computes it. A MOSI frame with a wrong CRC is not executed and sets ERRFL.CRC_error. A MISO frame with a wrong CRC fails the call with Error::Crc . Read and write sequences ¶ A read is two frames: the read command, then a NOP whose reply carries the data. When the reply's error bit is set, the driver reads ERRFL (two more frames, and the read clears it on the chip) to find out why. sequenceDiagram participant D as Driver participant C as AS5047U D->>C: read ANGLECOM (0x3FFF) C-->>D: reply to the previous frame (discarded) D->>C: read NOP (0x4000) C-->>D: ANGLECOM data, warning and error bits, CRC Note over D: error bit set? read ERRFL and fail the call A write is two frames, the command (RW = 0, address) and the data. The reply to the data frame reports on the command frame. With Verify::ReadBack , and always in EnsureInitialized() and ProgramOtp() , each write is then read back (two more frames) and compared. Brackets give the count with Verify::ReadBack . The two 350 ns limits are the ones a port can break: CSn low to the first clock edge, and CSn high between two frames. docs.text: "SPI Transaction" section, Figures 20 to 28. RW is 1 for a read and 0 for a write. Format MOSI (host to chip) MISO (chip to host) Driver 16 bit [14] RW = 1, [13:0] address [15] warning, [14] error, [13:0] data Bits16 : reads only, no CRC 24 bit [22] RW, [21:8] address or data, [7:0] CRC [23] warning, [22] error, [21:8] data, [7:0] CRC Bits24 : the default 32 bit [31:24] pad, then the 24-bit frame The 24-bit frame, then [7:0] pad Bits32 : daisy chains, pad from Config::pad_byte SPI frames, bit by bit Figure description and sources Each frame is drawn in the order it is clocked, most significant bit first, and the numbers above a row are bit positions in that frame. On MOSI the 16-bit command word holds the R/W bit (1 to read, 0 to write) and a 14-bit address; the data frame of a write has the same layout with R/W at 0 and the 14-bit value in place of the address. On MISO the reply word holds the warning bit, the error bit (a flag is set in ERRFL) and 14 data bits. The 24-bit frame adds the CRC-8 of the word in both directions. The 32-bit frame adds the pad byte: first on MOSI (the driver sends Config::pad_byte), last on MISO (the driver ignores it). The bit positions come from the frame constants in inc/as5047u_registers.hpp and the byte order from detail::FrameBus::Exchange in inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp. With 16-bit frames the driver sends writes as 24-bit frames. Drawn from: inc/as5047u_registers.hpp frame bits ; inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp detail::FrameBus::Exchange ; inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp Crc8 ; inc/as5047u.hpp writeFormat ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/spi-frames.py . The datasheet allows 16-bit frames for reads only, so with Bits16 the driver sends every write as a 24-bit frame. Writes are always CRC-protected, and ProgramOtp() sends every frame, reads included, as a 24-bit frame whatever Config::frame says, then restores the format. The CRC is CRC-8 with polynomial 0x1D, initial value 0xC4 and final XOR 0xFF, over the 16-bit word ("CRC Checksum"); as5047u::Crc8() computes it. A MOSI frame with a wrong CRC is not executed and sets ERRFL.CRC_error. A MISO frame with a wrong CRC fails the call with Error::Crc .

docs.text: A read is two frames: the read command, then a NOP whose reply carries the data. When the reply's error bit is set, the driver reads ERRFL (two more frames, and the read clears it on the chip) to find out why. sequenceDiagram participant D as Driver participant C as AS5047U D->>C: read ANGLECOM (0x3FFF) C-->>D: reply to the previous frame (discarded) D->>C: read NOP (0x4000) C-->>D: ANGLECOM data, warning and error bits, CRC Note over D: error bit set? read ERRFL and fail the call A write is two frames, the command (RW = 0, address) and the data. The reply to the data frame reports on the command frame. With Verify::ReadBack , and always in EnsureInitialized() and ProgramOtp() , each write is then read back (two more frames) and compared. Brackets give the count with Verify::ReadBack . Call Frames Clock time, 24-bit frames at 10 MHz ReadAngleCounts() and every other single read, reply with no flag bit 2 4.8 µs The same with a flagged reply (ERRFL read) 4 9.6 µs WriteRegister() 2 [4] 4.8 µs [9.6 µs] ReadNonVolatile() 14 33.6 µs ApplyConfig() , SetZeroPosition() , SetDirection() 26 [38] 62.4 µs [91.2 µs] EnsureInitialized() , chip already up 44 (20 with write_settings = false ) 105.6 µs (48 µs) EnsureInitialized() , chip not yet ready 2 more per poll, 1 ms apart, up to startup_timeout_ms SetZeroHere() 54 [78] 129.6 µs [187.2 µs] ProgramOtp() 100 at least, plus 2 per millisecond of burn time 240 µs plus the burn The times are derived (3 bytes of clock per frame), not measured. Add at least 350 ns of CSn high time per frame and your port's own overhead. A reply with the error bit set adds 2 frames for ERRFL.

docs.text: Figure 19. The two 350 ns limits are the ones a port can break: CSn low to the first clock edge, and CSn high between two frames. A hardware chip select usually meets them; a GPIO chip select toggled right next to the transfer may not. The deadline counts from the first poll, so raise it if your supply ramps slowly or the start comes before VDD is up. The only other wait is in ProgramOtp() , 1 ms between polls of the burn. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( as5047u_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-as5047u.git external/driver-as5047u git submodule update --init external/driver-as5047u Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-as5047u ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE as5047u::as5047u ) as5047u::as5047u is an alias of the as5047u INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect AS5047U_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver AS5047U_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-as5047u -B build-as5047u cmake --install build-as5047u --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( as5047u 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE as5047u::as5047u ) The target is as5047u::as5047u in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated as5047u_version.h go to include/as5047u/inc/ , the template implementation to include/as5047u/src/as5047u.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-as5047u) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-as5047u (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-as5047u.git components/as5047u as5047u (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml as5047u (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : as5047u : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-as5047u.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES as5047u (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/as5047u_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters Version ¶ The version is set once in the settings file and written into as5047u_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = as5047u :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0" Next ¶ Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

docs.text: Status and limitations ¶ What this driver has and has not been shown to do, so you can decide whether it is ready for your use. Status ¶ Version 0.1.0, not released On hardware Not verified. No board has run this driver yet Tested against A frame-level model of the chip ( Testing and CI ), a fuzzer and the quality gates Assurance level high (Kokeb Labs handbook): not qualified for use in a safety function What the model cannot show ¶ The host tests and the fuzzer run the driver against a model written from the datasheet, by the same reading of the datasheet as the driver. They prove the driver keeps its promises against that reading; they cannot prove the reading is right. In particular the model does not reproduce: the ECC algorithm of the OTP block (the model's checksum is a simple sum), the fuses or the guard-band level; the magnetic signal path: AGC, magnitude, DAEC and the velocity filter are values a test sets; any timing except the OTP burn time and the power-on time t_pon (a virtual clock): SPI timing and the 16-bit read latency need a bench; the DIA value before the loops settle (the datasheet gives none; the model reads some loops done) and whether two DIA reads in a row both report ready on a real part; what the settings registers read in their undescribed bits (DISABLE 13..7, the others 13..8, Figures 43 to 49): the model reads them as 0 and the reset compare ignores them; what ERRFL holds right after a power-on reset (the model sets OffCompNotFinished until t_pon has passed); whether the flag bits of the reply that carries ERRFL describe ERRFL before or after the read clears it (the driver accepts both, and refuses only a flag bit with ERRFL empty); which ERRFL flags set the reply's error bit and which its warning bit: the datasheet names both bits (Figure 22) and calls each flag an error or a warning (Figure 33), but gives no mapping. The driver therefore judges a flagged reply by ERRFL, not by which bit was set, and the model tests both readings; whether DIA bit 13 reads 0 (the datasheet leaves it undescribed, so the driver does not check it); the OTP burn time: the datasheet gives none, and kOtpBurnTimeoutMs (100 ms) is the driver's bound; how the chip treats the NOP read the driver sends after a failed transfer when a write was pending. The driver relies on the datasheet's frame rules (a data frame after a write command, 14 data bits), under which that frame writes 0; confirm it on a bench before relying on ProgramOtp() over an unreliable bus. What the driver cannot detect ¶ A reset of the chip that ERRFL does not report, or that changes nothing. The datasheet says a hardware reset loses the soft-written settings and reloads the OTP ("Non-Volatile Registers (OTP)"), and that OffCompNotFinished (ERRFL bit 9, Figure 33) is set while the offset compensation is not finished. It does not say that ERRFL holds that flag after a power-on reset, or for how long: the driver's automatic check (on OffCompNotFinished or WDTST after start-up) is a reading of Figure 33, not verified on hardware (bench step 4 in Testing and CI ). If a real part clears the flag before the next read, only CheckForReset() sees the reset: call it periodically (14 frames). Neither sees a reset that leaves the settings as they were (a configuration equal to the OTP), which loses nothing, or one between the check and the next read. The model raises the flag at every reset, so the host tests cannot show what the chip does. 16-bit frames carry no CRC. MISO stuck low, or a chip that hears MOSI as all zeros, reads as angle 0 with no flag bit; nothing in the frame tells it from a real 0. Floating high and looped-back lines are still caught. Use Bits24 (the default) wherever a stuck line must never read as a position. A write without read-back cannot see a looped-back MOSI : the echo of the data frame carries no flag. Writes that matter use Verify::ReadBack , and EnsureInitialized() and ProgramOtp() always read back. The datasheet asks for a DIA read after an error flag ("Volatile Registers", after Figure 33). The driver returns the error and leaves that read to the caller ( ReadDiagnostics() ), so the error path stays two frames shorter; confirm on a bench whether the chip needs it. Before you depend on it ¶ Run the bench check in Testing and CI on your board: a full turn of the magnet, the direction of the velocity sign, the AGC range, the start-up wait, the magnet warning and the line checks. Burn the OTP only on parts you can scrap until ProgramOtp() has been verified on hardware. Report what you found in an issue, with the board and the driver commit; a verified board is listed here. Hardware verification record ¶ Board Driver commit Procedure Result Evidence (none yet)

Neither sees a reset that leaves the settings as they were (a configuration equal to the OTP), which loses nothing, or one between the check and the next read. The model raises the flag at every reset, so the host tests cannot show what the chip does. 16-bit frames carry no CRC. MISO stuck low, or a chip that hears MOSI as all zeros, reads as angle 0 with no flag bit; nothing in the frame tells it from a real 0. Floating high and looped-back lines are still caught. Use Bits24 (the default) wherever a stuck line must never read as a position. A write without read-back cannot see a looped-back MOSI : the echo of the data frame carries no flag. Writes that matter use Verify::ReadBack , and EnsureInitialized() and ProgramOtp() always read back. The datasheet asks for a DIA read after an error flag ("Volatile Registers", after Figure 33). The driver returns the error and leaves that read to the caller ( ReadDiagnostics() ), so the error path stays two frames shorter; confirm on a bench whether the chip needs it.

EnsureInitialized() , ApplyConfig() and the setters write the volatile copy: it works at once and is lost at the next power cycle. Burning the OTP keeps it for good, and a chip can be burned once . docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the port. Datasheet sections this page relies on From ams OSRAM DS000637 v1-01: Power-up time and SPI timing: Timing Characteristics; SPI Timing, p. 9 SPI mode, frames and the read pipeline: SPI Interface (Slave); SPI Transaction, p. 16 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from as5047u::SpiInterface<Self> (in inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp ). The base uses CRTP and declares no hook itself; the driver template is constrained by the as5047u::SpiPort concept, so calls are resolved at compile time (no virtual functions, nothing to allocate) and a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use. The concept checks each hook's exact parameter types and noexcept : a Transfer() that takes a uint16_t length, or one without noexcept , does not satisfy it. What you implement ¶ Method Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept yes Bring the bus up on the first call; return true at once afterwards. false makes EnsureInitialized() return Bus bool Transfer(const uint8_t* tx, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t len) noexcept yes One full-duplex frame of len bytes (2, 3 or 4) with CSn low for all of them. rx is never nullptr : every frame carries a reply. false on any bus error void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept yes Wait at least us microseconds, never less: start-up polls DIA and ProgramOtp() polls the burn once per millisecond void Log(LogLevel, const char* message) noexcept no Print one line; message is plain text, never a format string The chip has no reset or interrupt pin, so there is no GPIO hook. CSn is the only control output: it idles high, and the port drives it high before it enables the pin as an output and before the first frame (handbook KB-HW-018). A port whose SPI peripheral drives CSn gets this from the peripheral; a port that drives CSn as a GPIO writes the level first, then sets the direction. The port ¶ my_port.hpp class MyPort : public as5047u :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One frame of 2, 3 or 4 bytes, CS low for all of them and high again afterwards. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: start-up polls DIA once per millisecond, ProgramOtp() the // burn. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules the transfer must follow: One call, one frame. Keep CSn low for all len bytes and raise it afterwards, for at least kMinCsHighNs . The chip executes a frame at the rising CSn edge and finds its length from the clocks in between, so two frames in one chip-select period are a framing error. The bus requirements below : mode 1, MSB first, up to kMaxClockHz . Start at 1 MHz on jumper wires. Full duplex. Clock tx out and fill rx with what the chip sends in the same frame. tx and rx are the driver's stack buffers, valid only during the call: a port that uses DMA copies them into DMA-capable memory it owns (handbook KB-HW-019). Raw bytes only. Do not interpret, retry or reorder bytes; the driver owns the framing, the CRC and the error handling. Return false for a bus error. The driver turns it into Error::Bus and never ignores it. Bounded time-outs. A stuck bus fails the call; it does not block forever. No other access between the two frames of a read. A read is the command frame and the NOP frame that carries the answer, inside one driver call (handbook KB-ARCH-043). On a shared bus, hold the bus lock for the whole driver call, not per frame. Bus requirements ¶ The driver states what the AS5047U needs from the bus as constexpr values in inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp (handbook KB-CPP-123). Check your port's settings against them with static_assert , as both example ports do, so a port that clocks too fast or in the wrong mode does not compile: Constant Value Meaning (datasheet "SPI Interface (Slave)", "SPI Timing", Figures 18 and 19) kSpiMode 1 CPOL 0, CPHA 1: MOSI sampled on the falling edge of CLK kMsbFirst true Most significant bit first kMaxClockHz 10'000'000 t_clk at least 100 ns kMinCsHighNs 350 CSn high between two frames, t_CSn (2 t_CLK_SYS + 10 ns) kCsSetupNs , kCsHoldNs 350 , 50 CSn falling edge to the first CLK rising edge, t_L; last CLK falling edge to CSn rising edge, t_H (t_clk / 2) kContinuousWord false Idle CLK time between the bytes of one frame is allowed; CSn must stay low kFrameBits {16, 24, 32} The frame lengths the chip accepts (Figures 20, 23, 26) The delay and the optional hook ¶ The driver finds the hooks beyond the bus at compile time, with named concepts in one place ( as5047u::detail : DeclaresDelayUs / HasDelayUs , DeclaresLog / HasLog ). A missing hook falls back in a documented, safe way or fails to compile; it never skips a step silently. A hook that is declared with the wrong signature ( DelayUs(uint16_t) , a Log without noexcept ) is a compile error, not a hook the driver quietly ignores. Hook Used for Without it DelayUs() 1 ms between polls of DIA at start-up and of the OTP burn in ProgramOtp() Compile error at EnsureInitialized() : the waits are required Log() One line per lifecycle event or failure Nothing is logged A port with every hook: class FullPort : public as5047u :: SpiInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return platform_spi_init (); } bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Required: start-up polls DIA, and ProgramOtp() the burn, once per millisecond. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( as5047u :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > as5047u :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } }; The start-up wait and the burn wait are requirements of the chip, so a port without DelayUs() is a compile error, not a start without waiting. The compile-fail tests check this rule, the exact hook signatures, and that a class which is not a port is rejected. Reference implementations ¶ Every port lives with its example, in examples/<platform>/ ; the driver has none. Platforms lists them and how to add one. examples/host/host_as5047u_port.hpp : any PC, against a simulated chip. Start from it for a host build or a test bench; it is also the smallest complete port. examples/esp32/main/esp32_as5047u_port.hpp : ESP-IDF, with every hook. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Call EnsureInitialized() : Ok proves that reads, writes and the CRC work and that an AS5047U answers and is ready. Call ReadAngleDegrees() twice a second and turn the magnet by hand: the angle follows it over the full turn. ReadAgc() should read well inside 0 to 255 with the magnet in place. With a scope on CSn and CLK, measure t_L, t_H and t_CSn at the clock you use against kCsSetupNs , kCsHoldNs and kMinCsHighNs ; and check that CSn is high from reset until the first frame. docs.text: Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the port. Datasheet sections this page relies on From ams OSRAM DS000637 v1-01: Power-up time and SPI timing: Timing Characteristics; SPI Timing, p. 9 SPI mode, frames and the read pipeline: SPI Interface (Slave); SPI Transaction, p. 16 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from as5047u::SpiInterface<Self> (in inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp ). The base uses CRTP and declares no hook itself; the driver template is constrained by the as5047u::SpiPort concept, so calls are resolved at compile time (no virtual functions, nothing to allocate) and a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use. The concept checks each hook's exact parameter types and noexcept : a Transfer() that takes a uint16_t length, or one without noexcept , does not satisfy it.
