docs.text: Method Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept yes Bring the bus up on the first call; return true at once afterwards. false makes EnsureInitialized() return Bus bool Transfer(const uint8_t* tx, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t len) noexcept yes One full-duplex frame of len bytes (2, 3 or 4) with CSn low for all of them. rx is never nullptr : every frame carries a reply. false on any bus error void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept yes Wait at least us microseconds, never less: start-up polls DIA and ProgramOtp() polls the burn once per millisecond void Log(LogLevel, const char* message) noexcept no Print one line; message is plain text, never a format string The chip has no reset or interrupt pin, so there is no GPIO hook. CSn is the only control output: it idles high, and the port drives it high before it enables the pin as an output and before the first frame (handbook KB-HW-018). A port whose SPI peripheral drives CSn gets this from the peripheral; a port that drives CSn as a GPIO writes the level first, then sets the direction.

docs.text: my_port.hpp class MyPort : public as5047u :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One frame of 2, 3 or 4 bytes, CS low for all of them and high again afterwards. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: start-up polls DIA once per millisecond, ProgramOtp() the // burn. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules the transfer must follow: One call, one frame. Keep CSn low for all len bytes and raise it afterwards, for at least kMinCsHighNs . The chip executes a frame at the rising CSn edge and finds its length from the clocks in between, so two frames in one chip-select period are a framing error. The bus requirements below : mode 1, MSB first, up to kMaxClockHz . Start at 1 MHz on jumper wires. Full duplex. Clock tx out and fill rx with what the chip sends in the same frame. tx and rx are the driver's stack buffers, valid only during the call: a port that uses DMA copies them into DMA-capable memory it owns (handbook KB-HW-019). Raw bytes only. Do not interpret, retry or reorder bytes; the driver owns the framing, the CRC and the error handling. Return false for a bus error. The driver turns it into Error::Bus and never ignores it. Bounded time-outs. A stuck bus fails the call; it does not block forever. No other access between the two frames of a read. A read is the command frame and the NOP frame that carries the answer, inside one driver call (handbook KB-ARCH-043). On a shared bus, hold the bus lock for the whole driver call, not per frame.

docs.text: The driver finds the hooks beyond the bus at compile time, with named concepts in one place ( as5047u::detail : DeclaresDelayUs / HasDelayUs , DeclaresLog / HasLog ). A missing hook falls back in a documented, safe way or fails to compile; it never skips a step silently. A hook that is declared with the wrong signature ( DelayUs(uint16_t) , a Log without noexcept ) is a compile error, not a hook the driver quietly ignores. Hook Used for Without it DelayUs() 1 ms between polls of DIA at start-up and of the OTP burn in ProgramOtp() Compile error at EnsureInitialized() : the waits are required Log() One line per lifecycle event or failure Nothing is logged A port with every hook: class FullPort : public as5047u :: SpiInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return platform_spi_init (); } bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Required: start-up polls DIA, and ProgramOtp() the burn, once per millisecond. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( as5047u :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > as5047u :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } }; The start-up wait and the burn wait are requirements of the chip, so a port without DelayUs() is a compile error, not a start without waiting. The compile-fail tests check this rule, the exact hook signatures, and that a class which is not a port is rejected.

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Run the driver on your PC first, with no hardware; then read the shaft angle from your MCU: wire the chip, place the magnet, write a small port class, call two driver functions. Datasheet sections this page relies on From ams OSRAM DS000637 v1-01: Pins and package: Pin Assignment, p. 3 Reference circuit: Circuit Diagram, p. 44 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Try it on your PC ¶ examples/host/ runs the real driver against a simulated AS5047U, through a host port. From the repository root, with CMake and a C++20 compiler: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example cmake --build build-example ./build-example/as5047u_host_example AS5047U driver 0.1.0 on the host as5047u: initialised angle 0.00 deg AGC 128 angle 29.99 deg AGC 128 angle 59.99 deg AGC 128 angle 90.00 deg AGC 128 The calls in main.cpp are the ones below; only the port differs on an MCU. CI builds and runs this example on every pull request. 1. Wire it ¶ 3.3 V mode: VDD and VDD3V3 tied together, so the logic levels match a 3.3 V MCU. MCU AS5047U Notes SPI SCLK CLK (pin 2) Mode 1 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 1), up to 10 MHz; 1 MHz for bring-up on jumper wires SPI MOSI MOSI (pin 4) SPI MISO MISO (pin 3) Chip select CSn (pin 1) Low for one frame, high between frames: one transfer per frame 3.3 V VDD (pin 11) and VDD3V3 (pin 12) 3.0 V to 3.6 V; 100 nF to GND close to the pins GND GND (pin 13) and TEST (pin 5) TEST must always be grounded Leave A, B, I, U, V and W open for this example. Centre a diametrically magnetised magnet (the datasheet's reference is 8 mm × 3 mm) over the package, close enough for 35 mT to 70 mT at the die. The Hardware page has the full pin list, the 5 V mode, the timing and the magnet limits. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the as5047u::as5047u CMake target. Installation covers CMake on any MCU, the installed package and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-as5047u.git external/driver-as5047u 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code: it brings the bus up and moves bytes. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp class MyPort : public as5047u :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One frame of 2, 3 or 4 bytes, CS low for all of them and high again afterwards. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: start-up polls DIA once per millisecond, ProgramOtp() the // burn. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Porting explains each method, the optional hooks and the transfer rules. 4. Read the angle ¶ main.cpp #include "as5047u.hpp" int read_shaft_angle ( MyPort & port , float & degrees ) { as5047u :: AS5047U < MyPort > sensor ( port ); // no I/O yet if ( auto r = sensor . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. bus up, wait for ready, Config{} written return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // Bus or NoDevice: check wiring, SPI mode 1 } const auto a = sensor . ReadAngleDegrees (); // 2. compensated angle, CRC-checked frame if ( ! a ) { return static_cast < int > ( a . error ); // MagnetWarning: magnet missing; DeviceFault: chip } degrees = a . value ; // 3. [0, 360), 14-bit resolution (0.022 degrees) return 0 ; } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() calls your port's EnsureInitialized() , clears ERRFL, checks that an AS5047U answers on MISO, and writes Config{} , the reset values of an unprogrammed part: 24-bit frames with CRC, clockwise, zero at 0, DAEC on. ReadAngleDegrees() reads ANGLECOM in two frames and checks the reply's CRC and error bit. The value is in degrees, [0, 360), at 14-bit resolution: 360° / 16384 = 0.022° per count. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. It is not verified on hardware yet. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check EnsureInitialized() returns Bus Your port's EnsureInitialized() : the bus did not come up EnsureInitialized() returns NoDevice , NotReady or DeviceIdMismatch MISO, MOSI, CSn, SPI mode 1, the supply and the magnet ( Troubleshooting ) Crc or Framing from any call Clock too fast for the wiring, or CSn not going high between frames ReadAngleDegrees() returns DeviceFault No magnet, or a chip fault: read ReadErrorFlags() and ReadDiagnostics() The angle does not follow the magnet Magnet off-centre or too far: check ReadAgc() ( Troubleshooting ) Next ¶ API guide : velocity, zero position, magnet health, errors. Configuration : every Config field, the ABI, UVW and PWM outputs, Kconfig. OTP programming : make the zero position and the settings permanent. Examples : the host example and the MCU examples. docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against a model of the chip, a fuzzer that corrupts what the chip sends back, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a frame-level model of the AS5047U: the reply to each frame answers the previous one, the frame length comes from the byte count, MOSI CRCs are checked, reading ERRFL clears it, writes take a command and a data frame, PROG runs the OTP state machine with a burn time, and DIA reports the loops finished only after t_pon on a virtual clock. Faults are injected per frame, per register or per line: a failed transfer, MISO stuck low or floating high, MOSI looped back to MISO, a chip that cannot hear MOSI, a chip that is late or never ready, a corrupted reply CRC, ERRFL flags (once, or persisting like a magnet out of range, and with either reading of which reply bit they set), writes that do not stick, a burn that never finishes, a failed guard-band test. They build as ISO C++20 ( CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF , -pedantic-errors , the C++20 deprecations as errors) with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang; the target as5047u_header_checks compiles each public header alone and asserts the dialect, and the Cortex-M cross-build compiles the same units. as5047u_host_tests runs 68 test cases; with the Kconfig, version, install, Doxygen, host-example, compile-fail and fuzz-corpus tests CTest runs 16 tests. cmake -S . -B build -DAS5047U_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_as5047u.cpp Validate() , unit conversions, NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() , settings written and read back at start-up, run-time writes sending no read-back by default and Verify::ReadBack catching a lost write, write_settings = false reading a burned part's settings (Data_select included) so a setter changes only its field, a missing chip in every frame format, every frame format with CRC-protected writes, reply CRC and error bit, warnings, PROG refused, measurements, direction, DAEC, SetZeroHere() , the OTP procedure and its failures (no confirmation, mismatch, timeout, guard band, device fault, CRC frames with 16-bit reads), logging tests/test_startup.cpp The start-up wait: no wait for a chip that is up, a poll per millisecond for a late one, NotReady at the deadline and never later, a ready DIA counted only when confirmed, the deadline bounded by Validate() ; each broken line (stuck low, floating high, looped back, deaf) refused at start-up in every frame format and on every read path after it tests/test_diagnostics.cpp The angle read is two frames; MagnetWarning for an angle or velocity under an AGC or magnetic-half warning, also when it persists, while diagnostic reads still answer; a P2RAM warning does not refuse it; the ERRFL latch fed by every read of ERRFL, internal ones included, until cleared; NoDevice for an error bit with no error and for ERRFL's reserved bit; GetLastReply() ; a chip that sets the error bit for warnings gives the same results, writes included tests/test_model.cpp The model's register map, fields, timing and CRC against the driver's, with static_assert ; the table CRC-8 against the bitwise one for all 65 536 words tests/test_bus_faults.cpp Every transfer of every read, configuration change, EnsureInitialized() and the OTP procedure fails in turn, and each returns Bus ; after any lost frame of ProgramOtp() no later call starts a burn, and a lost write frame never turns the next command into data tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( as5047u_fuzz_as5047u_corpus ), see below tests/test_reset.cpp A power-on reset of the model in mid-session (the settings reload from the OTP, t_pon restarts, ERRFL holds OffCompNotFinished): DeviceReset from the angle read, a setter and ReadErrorFlags() , during and after t_pon, and nothing written from the cache; docs.text: The driver is not verified on hardware yet. An MCU example ( Examples ) is the bench test: it logs angle, speed and AGC twice a second. Turn the magnet by hand through a full turn and check that the angle follows it from 0° to 360°, that the speed's sign follows the direction of rotation, and that the AGC stays well inside 0 to 255. Record the board and the result in the pull request's bench-status section. Test ProgramOtp() only on parts you can scrap. The start-up wait, the magnet warning and the line checks rest on the datasheet alone. Check each on the bench: Start-up wait. Power the sensor from a switchable supply and call EnsureInitialized() in the same moment; log GetLatchedErrorFlags() and count the DIA polls on a logic analyser. Expected: Ok within 10 ms, at least two DIA reads with LoopsFinished set before the first settings write. No magnet. Remove the magnet, start, and read the angle. Expected: NotReady at start-up or MagnetWarning on the angle read, never an angle; ReadAgc() near 255. Lines. With the driver running in Bits24 , disconnect MISO (pulled up, then pulled down), then MOSI, and read the angle. Expected: NoDevice (or Crc ), never a value. Bits16 frames have the limit described in Status and limitations . A reset of the chip. With the driver running, a configuration that differs from the OTP (a zero position other than 0) and the magnet still, cut the sensor's supply for 50 ms (or pull it below VDD minimum) and restore it while reading the angle every millisecond; log each result and GetLatchedErrorFlags() . Expected: the first read after the supply returns fails with DeviceReset (or NoDevice while the chip is unpowered), never an angle with the zero lost; CheckForReset() returns DeviceReset too. Record whether ERRFL held OffCompNotFinished on that first read: the driver's automatic check relies on it, the datasheet does not promise it. ERRFL after an error. Provoke a CRC error (a corrupted MOSI frame from a test port) and check that the next read returns Crc and that DIA reads normally afterwards, with and without a ReadDiagnostics() in between.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms, causes and fixes, cheapest check first. The causes are the datasheet's; none of them is verified on hardware with this driver yet. Datasheet sections this page relies on From ams OSRAM DS000637 v1-01: Power-up time and SPI timing: Timing Characteristics; SPI Timing, p. 9 CRC-8 of a frame: CRC Checksum, p. 23 Angle, velocity, AGC, magnitude, ERRFL and DIA registers: Volatile Registers, p. 24 AGC and the magnet's field strength: Automatic Gain Control (AGC) and CORDIC Magnitude, p. 37 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . EnsureInitialized returns Bus ¶ The port reported a failure: either EnsureInitialized() returned false or a transfer did. Check that your port's EnsureInitialized() returns true on its own (log it). Check the bus pins in your port against the board. With a logic analyser, check that the first frames (a read of DIA, command 0x7FF5) appear on the bus. EnsureInitialized returns NoDevice, NotReady or DeviceIdMismatch ¶ The driver polls DIA at start-up, once per millisecond up to Config::startup_timeout_ms (10 ms by default), and starts only when two DIA reads in a row report every magnetic loop finished. It then names what it saw last: Error What the bus showed Usual cause NoDevice All zeros or all ones (MISO stuck low or floating high), the looped-back command, or nothing but 0 in DIA No supply, MISO not connected, MOSI not reaching the chip NotReady A plausible DIA, but loops_finished never set No magnet or a far magnet, a slow supply ramp: raise startup_timeout_ms DeviceIdMismatch DIA with bit 10 set, which reads 0 on an AS5047U Another device on this chip select Crc Replies with a wrong CRC that are not line patterns Signal integrity, wrong SPI mode Cause Check Fix No supply, or TEST not grounded 3.0 V to 3.6 V (3.3 V mode) or 4.5 V to 5.5 V (5 V mode) on VDD; TEST at GND Fix the supply; ground TEST MISO not connected, or floating Probe MISO during a frame: it must toggle Wire MISO Wrong SPI mode Mode 1: CLK idles low, data sampled on the falling edge Set mode 1; modes 0, 2 and 3 do not work CSn held low across frames CSn must go high after each Transfer() One frame per chip-select period ( Porting ) 5 V mode with a 3.3 V MCU V_IH is 0.7 × VDD, 3.15 V at 4.5 V Level-shift, or run the sensor in 3.3 V mode Calls return Crc, Framing or Command ¶ Crc means a reply's CRC was wrong, or the chip saw a wrong CRC in a frame it received (ERRFL.CRC_error). Framing and Command come from ERRFL: the chip saw a frame of the wrong length, or an invalid command. Cause Fix Clock too fast for the wiring Drop to 1 MHz; the limit is 10 MHz on a short, clean bus CSn set-up or high time under 350 ns Add chip-select set-up and hold cycles in your SPI driver A frame of the wrong length Transfer() must clock exactly len bytes (2, 3 or 4) in one chip-select period Noise on CLK Shorter traces, a series resistor at the MCU, solid ground between MCU and sensor Command from ReadRegister() or WriteRegister() only The address does not exist on the chip Single errors point at signal integrity; an error on every call points at the port. With Bits16 reads carry no CRC, so a corrupted reply goes unnoticed: use Bits24 while you bring a board up. Reads return DeviceFault ¶ ERRFL reports a fault of the measurement path: P2RAM_error (uncorrectable OTP copy), Watchdog_error, Off_comp_error (offset compensation not finished) or CORDIC_overflow. The value is not a measurement. Read ReadErrorFlags() to see which flag it was. Off_comp_error or CORDIC_overflow right after power-up: EnsureInitialized() waits for DIA to report the loops finished, so this should not appear at start-up; GetLatchedErrorFlags() after start-up shows what the power-up left in ERRFL. Otherwise check the magnet: a missing or far magnet keeps the loops from settling ( ReadDiagnostics().value.loops_finished ). Either flag after start-up, or Watchdog_error, makes the driver compare the settings registers with what it wrote: DeviceFault means they were unchanged, so the chip was not reset or the reset lost nothing ( Calls return DeviceReset ). P2RAM_error or Watchdog_error that persists after a power cycle: replace the part. Calls return DeviceReset ¶ The chip lost its settings: a power-on reset or brown-out reloaded them from the OTP, which the driver saw as a difference in DISABLE to SETTINGS3 after ERRFL reported OffCompNotFinished or WDTST, or in CheckForReset() . The driver is uninitialised; nothing was written from its cache. Call EnsureInitialized() : it waits for the chip and writes the configuration again. Check the sensor supply for dips (decoupling at VDD and VDD3V3, the regulator, the connector) and the reset behaviour of whatever powers it. A DeviceReset with no supply event: a WriteRegister() or a write that the chip dropped (with Verify::None ) also leaves the registers differing from what the driver expects; use Verify::ReadBack to find it. Latched flags show flags_lost ¶ A read of ERRFL failed after the chip had cleared the register, so the flags it held were never seen. It follows a Crc , a Bus or a NoDevice from a call that read ERRFL: treat it as a fault that may have been missed, a reset of the chip included (its OffCompNotFinished may have been in the lost read). The driver compared the settings registers in that call when it could; to be sure, call CheckForReset() , read ReadDiagnostics() and ReadErrorFlags() , fix the signal integrity ( Calls return Crc, Framing or Command ), then ClearLatchedErrorFlags() . AGC at 0 or 255 ¶ AGC Meaning Fix Near 255, mag_half set Field too weak: magnet too far, too small or not diametrically magnetised Move it closer; the field must be 35 mT to 70 mT at the die Near 0 Field too strong Move the magnet away Changes with angle Magnet off-centre or tilted Centre it on the package axis ErrorFlags::agc_warning is set at either limit. An angle or velocity read under it fails with MagnetWarning ; the AGC, magnitude and diagnostics still read. GetLatchedErrorFlags() shows every warning the driver has seen, and ReadErrorFlags() reads ERRFL now. Reads return MagnetWarning ¶ The reply carried the warning bit and ERRFL holds AGC_warning or MagHalf: the field at the die is outside the range the chip regulates, so the angle is not a measurement (handbook KB-CPP-127). Fix the magnet as in the table above. The read cost four frames instead of two (the ERRFL read). While the field stays out of range, every angle read fails this way; nothing is returned as a value. Reads return NoDevice after a good start ¶ A reply that a stuck or looped-back line produces: all zeros or all ones with a wrong CRC, an ERRFL with its reserved bit set, or an error bit while ERRFL holds no error. Check that MISO is still driven and MOSI still reaches the chip; a connector that works loose does this. With Bits16 frames MISO stuck low reads as angle 0 with no flag ( Status and limitations ): use Bits24 . The angle is wrong or noisy ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Angle runs backwards Direction SetDirection(Direction::CounterClockwise) , or Config::direction Zero is in the wrong place Zero not set, or lost at power-off SetZeroHere() , then OTP programming to keep it Noisy at standstill High filter K, or DAEC at low speed Filter codes for a lower K ( filter_k_min_code , filter_k_max_code ); dynamic_compensation = false below about 100 rpm Lags at high speed DAEC off, or reading ANGLEUNC dynamic_compensation = true ; use ReadAngleCounts() The ABI count lags by a step after a reversal ABI hysteresis hysteresis_code (SETTINGS3.HYS, Figure 48) Velocity is not zero at standstill ¶ The velocity is a signed 14-bit value at 24.141 °/s per count. The datasheet gives 5.8 °/s rms noise at K = 0 and 244.9 °/s at K = 6 (Figure 17), so ±1 count with the magnet still is normal, and more with a high filter K. Detect "stopped" with a threshold, not with zero. Settings are gone after a power cycle ¶ The settings registers are volatile until the OTP is burned: this is expected. Write them in EnsureInitialized() at every start-up, or burn them once you are sure of them ( OTP programming ). A setting returns WriteMismatch ¶ A register read back different from what was written: a call with Verify::ReadBack , EnsureInitialized() or ProgramOtp() . Check for Crc errors on the same bus first; a read-only bit written through WriteRegister() also reads back differently. ProgramOtp fails ¶ OTP programming says what each failure means and whether the part can still be used.

Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/as5047u.hpp public calls ; inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Figure module: docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py Drawn from: public calls in inc/as5047u.hpp SpiInterface in inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp ProgramOtp(), step by step ¶ ProgramOtp(), step by step Figure description and sources The call first refuses to run when the driver is not initialised or the confirm value is wrong, and sends nothing then. It switches every frame to a CRC-protected format and runs three phases, top to bottom and left to right: prepare (steps 6 to 11: read the settings, compute and write the ECC key, read everything back and compare), burn (steps 12 to 14: enable programming, start the burn, poll PROG every millisecond until the burn is done or the timeout passes) and verify (steps 15 to 19: clear the volatile copy, reload it from the OTP at the guard-band level and compare it with what was burned). A pill on a step names the error that step adds; any step also fails on a transfer or reply error. The call stops at the first failure and OtpReport::failed_step names the step. OtpReport::burn_started becomes true just before the step 13 frame is sent, so from there on the fuses may be blown even if the call fails. The steps, registers, timeout and errors are read from otpPrepare(), otpBurn() and otpVerify() in src/as5047u.ipp. Drawn from: src/as5047u.ipp ProgramOtp ; src/as5047u.ipp otpPrepare ; src/as5047u.ipp otpBurn ; src/as5047u.ipp otpVerify ; inc/as5047u_types.hpp kOtpBurnTimeoutMs ; inc/as5047u_registers.hpp PROG and ECC ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/otp-flow.py . The chip answers a frame during the next one (dashed arrows), so a read sends the read command and then a NOP read, whose reply carries the register. The reply in the first frame belongs to the frame before it, so the driver fails the call there only when the transfer itself fails. When the reply that answers the call has its error bit set, the driver reads ERRFL (two more frames, dashed) to find out why and fails the call. A write sends the command frame (R/W at 0, the address) and the data frame, always with a CRC; the reply in the data frame reports on the command frame. The read-back after it (two more frames, dashed) is chosen per call with Verify::ReadBack; EnsureInitialized() and ProgramOtp() always read back. docs.text: ProgramOtp(), step by step Figure description and sources The call first refuses to run when the driver is not initialised or the confirm value is wrong, and sends nothing then. It switches every frame to a CRC-protected format and runs three phases, top to bottom and left to right: prepare (steps 6 to 11: read the settings, compute and write the ECC key, read everything back and compare), burn (steps 12 to 14: enable programming, start the burn, poll PROG every millisecond until the burn is done or the timeout passes) and verify (steps 15 to 19: clear the volatile copy, reload it from the OTP at the guard-band level and compare it with what was burned). A pill on a step names the error that step adds; any step also fails on a transfer or reply error. The call stops at the first failure and OtpReport::failed_step names the step. OtpReport::burn_started becomes true just before the step 13 frame is sent, so from there on the fuses may be blown even if the call fails. docs.text: Every access is two frames Figure description and sources Time runs left to right, one column per SPI frame; the top row is what the driver sends on MOSI and the bottom row what the chip returns on MISO in the same frame. The chip answers a frame during the next one (dashed arrows), so a read sends the read command and then a NOP read, whose reply carries the register. The reply in the first frame belongs to the frame before it, so the driver fails the call there only when the transfer itself fails. When the reply that answers the call has its error bit set, the driver reads ERRFL (two more frames, dashed) to find out why and fails the call. A write sends the command frame (R/W at 0, the address) and the data frame, always with a CRC; the reply in the data frame reports on the command frame. The read-back after it (two more frames, dashed) is chosen per call with Verify::ReadBack; EnsureInitialized() and ProgramOtp() always read back. The frame words come from readRaw(), writeRaw() and resolveFlags() in src/as5047u.ipp. A note at the bottom gives the rule of FrameBus::Exchange(): after a failed transfer the next frame is a NOP read, so a lost data frame cannot turn the next command into data.
